completed_unit.target: Cargo local-cache and network-preparation semantics relevant to offline vendoring
completed_unit.result: The pinned official cargo-fetch documentation states that when Cargo.lock exists, cargo fetch downloads the locked git and registry dependencies and makes them locally available; subsequent Cargo commands can run offline after cargo fetch unless the lock file changes. If Cargo.lock is absent, cargo fetch generates it before fetching. --locked asserts the existing exact dependency resolution and errors if the lock file is missing or would change, while --offline forbids network access and restricts Cargo to locally downloaded material; --frozen combines locked plus offline. Therefore Cargo.lock constrains dependency resolution but does not by itself populate the local cache: an online fetch or equivalent prior local materialization is still needed before offline operation for dependencies not already present.
